To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have used a new statistical method to analyze data from five previously reported chromosomes and that we have obtained strong evidence of linkage on chromosome 19 and weak evidence of linkage on another chromosome.
we found evidence for a second Alzheimer disease (AD) locus on chromosome 9 and that we found no evidence for a second AD locus on chromosomes 10, 12, 21, or 19p13.
we found strong evidence that LOFAD is a complex disease that is influenced by multiple genetic factors, and that we identified a second gene on chromosome 10 that influences LOFAD age at onset.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing methods to improve the power of linkage analysis in large pedigrees and to identify additional genes that contribute to the genetic etiology of late-onset AD.
the development of new methods for linkage analysis of complex diseases.
the development of novel methods to identify genes that cause complex genetic diseases, such as Alzheimer's disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a single major gene for LOFAD, APOE on chromosome 19, and that a second gene, on chromosome 19 at 19p13, is also likely.
we found evidence for a novel LOFAD locus on chromosome 10q and evidence for a second novel LOFAD gene locus on chromosome 12p.
there are at least two genes that influence age of onset of AD, one on chromosome 19 and one on chromosome 10.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the APOE locus accounts for 50%-75% of the genetic contribution to LOFAD, with the remaining 25%-50% due to a second major gene on chromosome 10 and several minor loci.

The main takeaway from our work is that
Bayesian methods for complex trait mapping are a powerful tool for identifying novel loci and that they can be applied to a wide range of complex traits.

Bayesian Markov chain Monte Carlo linkage analysis is a promising approach for the analysis of LOFAd in large pedigrees and that the use of covariates, such as APOE genotype, in linkage analysis can be a powerful way to improve power to detect additional LOFAD genes.
